newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - July 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - July 25.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- APPLE DAILY -- The Independent Commission Against Corruption arrested 15 people on suspicion of taking bribes collectively from housing subcontractors.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- Chinese President Jiang Zemin and Premier Li Peng stressed that China was politically stable and the leadership was united and capable.

-- After Guangzhou decided to let foreign investors be involved in building its new airport, more than 50 consortiums from different countries have arrived in the city to seek cooperation opportunities.
-- SING TAO -- Chinese President Jiang Zemin asked those in charge of drafting his work report for the 15th Communist Party Congress to ignore the arguments of left-wing cadres.

-- APPLE DAILY -- The former director of China's Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office, Lu Ping, was forced to retire ahead of schedule because he took a more lenient attitude towards the Democratic Party, against the view of the director of the New China News Agency Hong Kong branch, Zhou Nan.
-- TIN TIN -- A bank in Guangdong's Jieyang city closed owing 200 million yuan to depositors due to the corruption of its boss, who had bought the position for 350,000 yuan.

-- MING PAO -- A book by the son of China's Foreign Minister Qian Qichen, "Studying in America", is a bestseller in China. Qian Zhou said only when he arrived in the United State did he realise the possibility of such a different way of life.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Solicitor-General Daniel Fung admitted the provisional legislature did not fulfil requirements laid out for the establishment of the post-handover government's first law-making body.

-- Hong Kong jumped to fifth place in the rankings of the world's top foreign exchange reserves, with the first-time inclusion of the Land Fund boosting its total to more than US$82 billion at the end of June.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Chinese Premier Li Peng threw his weight behind President Jiang Zemin as the 15th Party Congress approaches.
